items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah, you don’t get Taa, you kind of get a little—

ctx.x: It wasn’t particularly much fun to play, that particular instrument, but I mean it did work that way, if they needed it to blend in with the strings. Because the strings, I mean, it’s just a fact of life that they play just that little bit behind because of the conductor.
Yeah, you don’t get Taa, you kind of get a little—

You can get that if you tell them ahead of time, I mean the good string players, like the guys that do the studios and also the symphonies and all that, I mean if you say I want it when my hand hits the belt buckle, I mean I want boom here, rather than, daaa, on the upbeat, well they’ll come through for you, because they’re all good musicians.
